editorial:
Ever wonder how some people manage to climb to the top by being the biggest jerk in the room? You get a front-row seat to that exact lifestyle with this look at Roy Cohn. He was the ultimate power player in New York, acting as the right-hand man for Senator McCarthy and later becoming a mentor to Donald Trump. The movie feels like a deep dive into the mind of a man who lived by one rule: never lose, no matter how many people you have to step on. It is a wild ride that shows how he manipulated the law and the government to protect himself and his powerful friends while destroying anyone who got in his way.

What really makes this work is how it uses old footage and interviews to paint a picture of a man who was terrified of appearing weak. The pacing is quick, and the revelations about his secret personal life add a layer of irony to his public persona. If you like true crime or political drama, you will find this fascinating.
endingExplained: The film wraps up by showing Roy Cohn's lonely and painful end. Despite all his power and money, he dies from AIDS at a time when the disease was a huge social taboo. He spent his final days denying his illness and trying to keep his secrets safe. The movie ends by showing how his legacy of bullying and lying lived on through the people he taught, leaving you to think about the cost of his greed.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves political scandals and true crime stories.
